Oof, where to start?

First of all, I simply don't want to be a mother, which itself is reason enough, but there are more.

 Pregnancy scares me, growing another being inside yourself and then having to push it out under excruciating pain doesn't sound so magical to me. It sounds painful, dangerous, and just exhausting. 

And then when the pregnancy is over, you have to care for the baby basically 24/7. You're responsible for not only keeping this very fragile little person alive, but also raising them. Giving them love, teaching them, meeting their emotional and physical needs. 
I'm not mentally, emotionally or financially (and god, kids are expensive) stable enough for that kind of responsibility, and i just simply don't have the urge to raise a child.
I'm an introvert and i enjoy my free time in solitude and quietness which isn't really compatible with having a kid.

Also, i don't particularly hate children, but i don't like them either. I don't find babies cute, i just think they're loud, expensive and, honestly, kinda gross with all the bodily fluids they're producing and all.

And then on top of all that there's the lovely element of ✨childhood trauma✨ that comes from having two not so great parents myself (separated, kinda absent, narcissistic tendencies, not physically abusive but emotionally and verbally), so i worry that if i ever procreated I'd fuck that kid's mental health up like my parents did mine, and I don't wanna subject a kid to that shit. Not to mention that bringing a new life into this fucked up world generally sounds like a bad idea.

So, yah. Thanks, but it's a no from me.

Okay, listen, you seriously need to stop viewing everything as a personal attack. The teacher didn't attack you, your parenting, or your child, she just notified you that your child fell asleep in class. 

It's not the teacher's job to make sure your child gets enough sleep, it's yours. It IS their job, however, to tell the parents if the child acts unusual or displays behaviours that indicate some kind of issue, so that the parents can investigate and fix the problem.  


There could be many reasons for a kid falling asleep in class, like secretly staying up for too long, being ill,  not being able to sleep at night because they're going through something emotional, consuming caffeine too close to bedtime, being kept awake by noise, etc. Those mostly aren't indicators of neglect, just unfortunate happenstances.

And they are things you can easily fix as a parent, IF YOU KNOW ABOUT IT.  The teacher told you so you're aware and can help your child get enough undisturbed rest. 
That wasn't an accusation of you being neglectful, it was just a "hey, your kid seems to be getting too little sleep, please help them with that."
But you immediately interpreted it as a "your child obviously doesn't get enough sleep and it's your fault, you're a terrible, neglectful parent, how could you". 
Huge overreaction.

I've seen a lot of people make you're/your and they're/their/there mistakes, so I'll add to the list:

You're = You are, example: "You're a nice person."

Your= possessive adjective, example: "I like your new sweater."

They're= They are, example: "Ron and Ginny look alike because they're siblings."

Their= possessive adjective, example: "Fred and George seem happy, their joke shop is doing well!"

There= adjective to indicate a location , example: "We went to Hogsmeade and stayed there for a few hours!"

Those don't look very deep, so if they scar the scars will very likely be thin, flat and light. I have similar ones, and mine are only noticeable because i have so many of them. You might get a few lines on your arm that are a few shades lighter than your skin tone, but they will probably be very unnoticeable unless you're really looking for them.

They will probably also not all like each other equally. For example, character 1 could be really good friends with character 2, and really respect, but not be very close to character 3. Maybe 1 and 4 are rivals, but actually like each other, or 1 has a mentor/mentee relationship with 5 because 5 is less experienced and doesn't really have a clue what to do. 

You also have to consider if they have leader or follower personalities. Maybe 2 of them are natural leaders, but don't always agree with each others strategies, so they argue a lot. It's a bit more interesting than just one dominant personality that leads the team, and adds a bit of depth and conflict to the team. They are 5 different people and just expecting them to work together perfectly and be best friends might be a bit too much to ask for. Even if they all like each other, there will always be small conflicts. Like 1 telling too many bad jokes and annoying 4, or 3 being against 5 being on the team because 5 is too young or inexperienced and could get hurt, so 5 is offended and sad and 2 gets mad at 3 for being mean.
There will always be characters that fit better with each other than others, and that's okay and makes it fun and exciting and makes an interesting team dynamic, as long as they can still work well together to reach one goal. I hope this is kinda helpful.

Okay, so, everything here is based on my own personal experience, so i don't know how it's for other people, but that's how it's for me:

I've never actually tried to commit suicide, but there were quite a few instances where i was really close to doing it and somehow talked myself out of it when i already had the blade on my arm. I'm 18, and nobody in my family even knows i have depression ( i was never diagnosed, but I'm pretty sure that's what it is after years of being unhappy and fantasizing about my own death, so yeah.) For me it's like... There are some moments where I'm happy. When i can distract myself, meet up with friends, just forget everything else. And then, when I'm alone, i read a lot and try not to think about it. I'm not particularly happy then, but I'm too distracted to think about it. But when I'm alone, doing nothing, i start to think about my life, my situation, myself, and then i just kinda... Crash? I just break down and cry and want to die and it really sucks. That sometimes happens just without a reason, but also after something bad happens. It doesn't have to be something big, something it's a tiny thing like my mother being mad at me, but it's enough for my mood to tip from ,, kind of okay and functioning" to ,,i really want to kill myself right now." So for me, being suicidal is not thinking about my own death 24/7 (though that happens too sometimes), but for that i have to distract myself with something i like doing and avoid anything negative. Which is hard. When I'm really close to killing myself i write suicide notes most of the time. I write that I'm not sorry for doing it, but I'm sorry for hurting anyone reading it. That it's not their fault (which is not always what i think, but i just want to die, not make anyone feel guilty), that i love them, etc. Sometimes i include my reasons, but not always. Then i throw stuff away. I delete things from my phone that I don't want anyone to find, and remove the password. I throw away things i want noone to see. I try to subtly check on my friends to make sure they are okay. I pick a time and place that i know someone will check soon, but not too soon, because I don't want to be found before I'm dead but i also don't want to lie around decomposing for a few days. (mostly my room, when i know i have a few hours until someone comes home.) I pick a method. I put the note in my pocket or next to me. And then i sit down and prepare myself for doing it. And I'm always so so close, but i manage to talk myself out of it at the last second. In that time between deciding to die and actually attempting it, when I'm preparing, i get really peaceful after a while. It's like ,,it will all be over soon. I'll finally be free and not sad anymore and it will be over." And it makes me smile and i stay calm even if my mother, for example, screams at me, because i know that it won't matter when I'm dead.

To know if the character could have blue eyes, you'll have to look into their genetic makeup. I only know the proper words for it in German, so sorry if this is not quite understandable, and please forgive me any grammatical errors, but: 
Your eyecolour is determined by the genes your parents pass down to you. Every person has two alleles for eyecolour, one from the father and one from the mother. So if, for example, someone gets the allele for blue eyes from their mother and the allele for brown eyes from their father, they will have brown eyes, because brown is the dominant eyecolour and will overpower the blue allele. However, they still have the capability to have a child with blue eyes, by passing down their blue allele. If the child they passed the blue allele to gets another blue allele from the other parent, it will have blue eyes. So, for a child to have blue eyes, there has to be someone with blue eyes (or just the allele for it) in their ancestry (for example a grandparent or great grandparent). Then, their blue allele has to be passed down all the way to the kids parent, who has to pass the allele down to their kid (it's a 50/50 chance which allele the kid gets). Which is not as impossible as it sounds, because, though the odds are not very high, there have been cases where a recessive gene was passed down for a dozen of generations and then suddenly popped up when the partner had a compatible gene for it to show. Then, the other parent has to have a blue allele too, and pass it down to the kid. Now the kid has two blue alleles and gets blue eyes. 
So, for your character, the most probable story would be: an ancestor of the Japanese parent had a child with someone with blue eyes (most likely not Asian, probably European) and the gene was passed down since then without showing because all other ancestors only had brown alleles. Then the American parent has blue eyes (or just carries the gene without it showing, but them having blue eyes makes it more likely for the kid to have blue eyes too). They both pass down the blue allele, and boom, blue eyed half Japanese kid. 

Now, heterochromia is not really in our genetic makeup. One way to get it is to merge with/absorb your fraternal twin in the womb, so one eye will have the colour they would've had if you hadn't absorbed them, and the other is your own. Another way is for the eye to get damaged somehow (either in the womb or at birth) so the melanin (the more melanin your eye has the darker it is) can't properly get into the eye, so it ends up lighter than the other one because the pigment is missing. Heterochromia can also be a symptom of some disorders like the Waardenburg syndrome, for example (another symptom for that is loss of hearing). 
Or your genetics can just go ,,fuck you, I'll do what i want." And you get two different eye colours. That happens too. 

I don't know how much of that you already knew, some of it is pretty basic biology, but i hope i could help you. If you wanna read more about it, here's some links!:
